title: Accept the GitHub squash identity in the privacy gate
body:
`main` fails the privacy gate at `18d73783`, and so does every branch based on it. The gate exempts exactly one squash commit, `ae982af`. Every later pull request is squash-merged on GitHub, so its commit carries the account's noreply author and GitHub as committer, and the gate refused it.

- `scripts/check_privacy.py` accepts exactly two identity pairs: the holder identity as author and committer, and the GitHub squash pair (the account's noreply author with GitHub as committer). Every commit needs a one-line message. The exact `ae982af` exception and the content scan are unchanged.
- `commit_errors()` holds the whole per-commit check. `check_privacy.py --selftest` runs it on 11 commit controls:
  - pass: the holder pair, the squash pair, the exact owner squash;
  - fail: a mixed pair, the holder author with the GitHub committer, another account's noreply address, the reversed pair, a case variant, and a multi-line message on either accepted pair.
  `validate.py` runs it, and the gate refuses unknown arguments.
- [IMPORT.md](docs/IMPORT.md), [VERIFICATION.md](docs/VERIFICATION.md) and CHANGELOG describe the rule.
- The repository now allows squash merges only, with the PR title as subject and a blank body.

Validation:
- all 24 `validate.py` gates pass with GoogleTest 1.14.0 and Clang 18;
- R562-1's planted-fault probe: all 9 faults fail `--selftest`, and the control passes;
- the bare-metal job is unaffected (scripts and docs only).

Blocks tsn-c-stack #14: its branch fails the privacy gate only because of this.
